August 23, 2026

Trump made more than 1,000 stock trades in June, ethics filing shows

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

A new filing with the Office of Government Ethics shows Donald Trump executed more than 1,000 stock trades in June, valued at between $78 million and $263 million. Over the past 18 months, the total value of trades attributed to him exceeds $1 billion. Trump has previously said he supports banning congressional stock trading and maintains there are no ethics issues with his own trades, though some involve companies he deals with directly as president.

White House trains officials on subpoena responses ahead of expected investigations

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The White House is preparing for a wave of congressional investigations and possible impeachment proceedings, and has begun instructing cabinet secretaries and other federal officials on how to respond to subpoenas and active inquiries. The Wall Street Journal reported that Democrats have assembled an extensive investigation plan should they take control after the November elections. The preparations cover alleged misdeeds and corruption across the administration and various cabinet departments.

ICE agents attempt hospital arrest of Ecuadorian mother and daughter after crash in Florida

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

ICE agents sought to detain a 39-year-old mother and her 19-year-old daughter, both from Ecuador, at HCA Florida Poinciana Hospital in Kissimmee after another driver caused a near-fatal crash involving the two. Footage shows agents attempting to separate the pair, with the mother dragged from the hospital room. Relatives said the daughter was suffering a seizure at the time.

One-year-old appears alone in Arizona immigration court and is told to file asylum claim

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting from Notice confirms that a one-year-old child appeared in immigration court in Arizona this week without a parent, and the judge instructed the child to file an asylum claim. An attorney from the U.S. Committee for Refugees, one of the groups contracted by the Department of Homeland Security to represent migrant children, was present but did not speak during the hearing. The case reflects the circumstances facing unaccompanied minors in the immigration court system.

CBP agent detains man at Florida gas station, citing his immigrant status

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Footage from a gas station in Florida shows a Customs and Border Protection agent approaching and detaining a man. When the man asked why he was being stopped, the agent responded that it was because he was an immigrant, then placed his hands behind his back and arrested him. The encounter has been characterized as racial profiling.

Canada rejects trade deal as premiers float tariffs aimed at Trump-voting states

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Prime Minister Mark Carney broke off a trade arrangement Trump had claimed was in place, saying the proposals put forward were not in Canada's interests and that Canada has other trading partners available. Canadian politicians including Premier Doug Ford have suggested targeting retaliatory tariffs only at U.S. states that voted for Trump, sparing states that did not. The dispute has produced unusual cross-party unity in Canada as the trade war escalates.

Trump photographed at headshot session amid war with Iran and trade dispute

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The Team Trump account posted images over the past 24 hours appearing to show the president having new headshots taken. The timing was noted against the backdrop of the ongoing war with Iran, the trade conflict with Canada, and rising domestic prices. It is unclear exactly when the images were captured.

Reports describe settler attacks on Palestinian farmers and water supplies in West Bank

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

Accounts circulating from the South Hebron Hills describe Israeli settlers taking a donkey from a Palestinian farmer and dragging it until it died. In the Jordan Valley, armed settlers were reported to have emptied Palestinian water tanks, cutting off families' water supply during extreme heat. The reports were presented alongside criticism of U.S. military aid to Israel and the level of U.S. national debt, and alongside social media content from Israeli figures mocking shortages of water and power in Gaza.

Archive of alleged war-crime footage from Gaza said to run to 2,000 hours

tags: war, media
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A website has compiled what is described as more than 90 days of continuous footage, roughly 2,000 hours, documenting alleged atrocities against Palestinians. The material was presented as evidence to counter claims that the reported abuses are exaggerated. The account noted that the archive has received no mainstream media coverage and described the content as extremely graphic.

Utah Senate candidate says Curtis's office refused meeting and called criticism 'bad behavior'

tags: politics, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

Caroline Gleich, who ran against John Curtis for the U.S. Senate in Utah in 2024, published an account of asking for a meeting with the senator-elect in December 2024. She says chief of staff Corey Norman replied that they were "full," sent screenshots of her social media posts, and said her criticism was "bad behavior" he would not "reward," and that Curtis scolded her at an airport baggage claim that same week. She cites Heritage Action scores of 94% for this session and 89% lifetime, and a FiveThirtyEight finding that Curtis voted with Trump's position 94% of the time in the House, arguing his environmental voting record is now worse than Mike Lee's.

Claims that US horses are being routed overseas for slaughter as beef imports expand

tags: politics, markets
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Claims circulating allege the Trump administration has used a loophole to send American horses overseas for slaughter, avoiding domestic prohibitions on the practice. The claims were raised alongside reporting that the administration is importing hundreds of billions of dollars of foreign beef at a 25% discounted rate. No official confirmation of the horse export program was cited.

Doctors said to be concerned about Trump's weight gain

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Washington Post reported growing concern among doctors about Donald Trump's weight, which is said to have increased by 20 to 23 pounds since he took office. The concern centers on his age of 80 and his diet. The report links the weight gain to a broader decline in his health over roughly the past 18 months.

Holocaust memoir author admitted concentration camp apple story was invented

tags: media, history
sources: @ericmoutsos

Herman Rosenblatt gained international attention for a story about being given apples by a girl outside a Nazi concentration camp fence, whom he later said he met on a blind date and proposed to on the spot. The account brought him and his wife Roma onto Oprah twice, along with book and movie deals, before it was shown to be false, with Roma's family having been more than 200 miles away at the time. Rosenblatt said he fabricated the story to give people hope, while family members said the motivation was money.
